A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the first law analysis showed that the system is thermodynamically feasible.
the authors have developed a new correlation for the specific entalpy of the ammonia/ammonium salt solutions for the whole range of concentration and temperature.
the authors have developed a model to calculate the performance of a single stage absorption refrigeration system with ammonia/salt mixtures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the second law efficiency of the system can be increased up to 20% by using a heat recovery system, which is the main focus of the work and not the specific enthalpies of the solutions.

the second law efficiency is higher for the ammonia/salt absorption systems than for the conventional vapour compression systems and the first law efficiency is higher when using LiNO3 as the absorbent.

the second law efficiency of the absorption refrigeration cycle depends strongly on the thermodynamic properties of the working fluids and on the operating conditions of the heat exchangers and of the generator.
